title: Turkey, light or dark meat, smoked, skin edible

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a large bird native to North America. Smoked turkey meat, both light and dark, has a rich smoky aroma, tender texture, and distinctive flavor. The skin left on after smoking is edible and adds a crunchy element to the dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkeys can weigh over 20 lb, but most commercial birds are 6–11 lb.
Smoking uses wood smoke to impart flavor and extend shelf life.
Light meat (breast) contains less fat than dark meat (thighs, drumsticks).
Turkey skin is rich in collagen, which becomes crisp when properly cooked.
Smoked turkey is traditionally served in the United States during Thanksgiving.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Smoked turkey provides about 29 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low fat in light meat
items.content: Turkey breast is very low in saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey is a good source of niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, which support bone health and immunity.

items.title: Antioxidant smoke compounds
items.content: Wood smoke contains polyphenols that may provide modest antioxidant effects.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Smoked products often contain high levels of salt, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial risk
items.content: Undercooked turkey may harbor salmonella; ensure the meat reaches a safe internal temperature.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bird proteins.

items.title: Caloric skin
items.content: The skin is higher in fat and calories, so it should be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice smoked turkey thinly for salads, sandwiches, appetizers, or as a main course. The skin can be crisped in a pan and added to soups or salads for texture. Cold slices pair well with mustard, cranberry sauce, or a light yogurt dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep smoked turkey in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or slimy texture; discard if any signs of spoilage are present.
